P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No foreign exchange controls (Deloitte 2026): the remaining exchange controls on capital movements were lifted when the Australian dollar was floated in December 1983 (Reserve Bank of Australia). Receiving foreign payments is unrestricted; AUSTRAC reporting applies to international transfers and large cash amounts (not captured).

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes, but bank foreign-currency accounts for individuals can need large balances. BankSA's (Westpac group) Foreign Currency Account is available to individual and business customers aged 18+, with a minimum opening balance for individuals equivalent to AUD 50,000, at the bank's discretion. At CommBank, some currencies are available only on its Business Foreign Currency Account. Fintech multi-currency accounts are the usual low-cost alternative (see P5).

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Sole traders register for an Australian Business Number (ABN), a free 11-digit identifier issued through the Australian Business Register (managed by the ATO), if they are running a business. An ABN lets you avoid PAYG withholding on payments you receive and claim GST credits. Business name registration is separate and only needed when trading under a name other than your own (not captured).

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents are taxed on worldwide income, except certain foreign income of temporary residents; non-residents only on Australian-source income. Residence includes being in Australia for more than half the income year (183 days), among other tests. Progressive rates apply, plus the Medicare levy (see below). ATO resident rates 2025–26: nil up to AUD 18,200; 16% to 45,000; 30% to 135,000; 37% to 190,000; 45% above. The 2% Medicare levy is extra. For 2026–27 the 16% band falls to 15%. Sole traders (with an ABN) are taxed on business profit at these individual rates (not quoted).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: GST is 10%. A business must register when GST turnover reaches AUD 75,000 (AUD 150,000 for non-profits), within 21 days of becoming aware it will exceed the threshold; voluntary registration is allowed below it. Exports are GST-free (zero-rated), including many services to non-residents.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Australian Consumer Law (ACL) consumer guarantees apply equally to online, in-store and sale purchases. If a product fails a guarantee, you must provide a remedy. For a minor failure you choose repair or replacement. For a major failure the consumer chooses, including a refund, even if the item is out of its packaging. You also pay return shipping for faulty goods. You are NOT obliged to give change-of-mind refunds unless your policy offers them, and online sellers can set their own change-of-mind terms. Blanket 'no refunds' wording that implies guarantees do not apply is risky (ACCC view per secondary sources, not captured).

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: Small business income tax offset (unincorporated small business tax discount): sole traders with aggregated turnover under AUD 5 million get 16% of the tax on their net small business income, up to AUD 1,000 a year. The ATO calculates it automatically from your return. TRAP for freelancers: personal services income (income mainly for your own personal effort or skill) does not count unless you are a personal services business, so many solo contractors get little or no offset (ATO).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: none of the major platform barriers apply. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Physical or digital goods on Etsy (Etsy seller payments are available here). (6) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Fully localized'). (7) Stripe accepts merchants here, so you can take card payments directly on your own site. (8) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
